Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) centrally governs IPN: state-owned by CBE; CBE is system owner/overseer/settlement agent and sets regulations (CBE board approves fee grids, limits, security standards). Day-to-day execution is through Egyptian Banks Company (EBC), CBE’s technical subsidiary, with an EBC board including CBE and bank representatives. ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 IPN Egypt case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips2025/siips_2025_IPN-Egypt_CaseStudy_en.pdf))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and corroborated: a March 2026 practitioner guide (ClearingPost) independently describes IPN as CBE-operated national infrastructure launched under a 2020 CBE mandate, run day-to-day by CBE's own subsidiary EBC — consistent with the AfricaNenda account of direct CBE ownership/oversight and EBC operation. Value 5 (Direct Operation) confirmed.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Mandatory breach notification: PDPL requires controllers/processors to notify the competent authority within 72 hours of a personal data infringement (immediately if national security-related) and notify affected data subjects within 3 days after notifying the authority. ([DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World – Egypt](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?t=law&c=EG))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Strongly confirmed with independent corroboration: the ICLG Data Protection Report 2025-26 and a January 2026 English translation of the PDPL's Executive Regulations both confirm Article 7 of Law 151/2020 requires notification to the Data Protection Centre within 72 hours (immediate for national-security matters) and to affected data subjects within three days. Value 3 (Mandatory) confirmed, this being a general data-protection duty applicable to payment data controllers/processors rather than a payments-specific rule.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Evidence of inclusion-oriented governance: the National Payments Council sets national payments strategy and includes financial-inclusion goals; CBE mandated zero fees for P2P/P2B through IPN/InstaPay for 3 years (until Apr 2025) and introduced capped low fees afterward to keep small-value transactions affordable; IPN design uses proxy identifiers (mobile numbers/IPA) and interoperates across banks/wallets/cards to broaden access. ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 IPN Egypt case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips2025/siips_2025_IPN-Egypt_CaseStudy_en.pdf))

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Egypt has a national Instant Payment Network (IPN) launched in March 2022, providing 24/7 real-time interoperable transfers and payments; IPN connects bank accounts, mobile wallets, and cards and is accessed by the InstaPay app; by 2024 IPN processed ~1.561B transactions ($92B value) and had 12.72M unique users. ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 IPN Egypt case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips2025/siips_2025_IPN-Egypt_CaseStudy_en.pdf))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Strongly confirmed and corroborated: CBE's PAFIX conference remarks (17 Nov 2025) report over 16 million InstaPay users and c.1.1 billion transactions worth EGP 2.4 trillion since the March 2022 nationwide launch, mandatory across all licensed banks; independently consistent with AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 and a March 2026 payments-infrastructure guide. Value 5 (Fully deployed nationwide) confirmed.
